answer: Random-walk landing probability resists sybils: short random walks launched from a trusted seed set terminate mostly on honest, well-connected nodes; a sybil region attached through few edges receives walkers only rarely, so its landing probability is near-hollow. The forge of trust is the seed, and weight is the chance a walk from it ends on you. A fake voyage of thousands behind a thin cut collects almost no landing mass however densely they interlink, because walkers seldom cross the bottleneck to reach them.
